question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 16.02, an "approved form" is a contractual or conveyance form that:
choice_a: Has been prepared and approved by the Real Estate Examining Board, or is listed in REEB 16.03
choice_b: Any licensee may draft and self-approve for use in a transaction
choice_c: Is approved solely by the buyer and seller's own agreement
choice_d: Must be approved by a court before every use
explanation: REEB 16.02 defines an "approved form" as a contractual or conveyance form prepared and approved by the Real Estate Examining Board, or listed among the forms approved under REEB 16.03.

question: Which of the following is among the form categories the Real Estate Examining Board approves under REEB 16.03?
choice_a: Any form a title company chooses to draft on its own
choice_b: State Bar of Wisconsin forms for deeds, mortgages, mortgage notes, land contracts, and releases
choice_c: Forms drafted by an unlicensed assistant
choice_d: Verbal agreements memorialized after closing
explanation: REEB 16.03 approves specific form categories, including State Bar of Wisconsin forms for deeds, mortgages, mortgage notes, land contracts, and releases, certain UCC forms, out-of-state transaction forms, government-agency forms, and broker/attorney/landlord-drafted property management agreements.

question: Under REEB 16.04, when must a Wisconsin real estate licensee use an approved form?
choice_a: Only if the client requests it in writing
choice_b: Only for commercial transactions
choice_c: Whenever acting as an agent or a party to a real estate transaction of a type for which an approved form exists
choice_d: Only when no attorney is involved in the transaction
explanation: REEB 16.04 requires licensees to use approved forms when acting as an agent or a party to a real estate transaction for which an approved form exists -- this is the rule that makes a WB-series offer to purchase the required vehicle for a residential purchase offer.

question: Under REEB 16.04, if no board-approved form exists for a particular type of transaction, a licensee may use:
choice_a: A form the licensee personally drafts and signs as the source
choice_b: No written form at all; the transaction must proceed orally
choice_c: Any form found online, regardless of its source
choice_d: A contractual form drafted by a party or an attorney, provided the drafter's name is imprinted on the form
explanation: REEB 16.04 permits use of a contractual form drafted by a party or an attorney for transaction types with no approved form, as long as the drafter's name is imprinted on the form.

question: Under REEB 16.05, a real estate licensee generally may NOT:
choice_a: Give advice or opinions concerning the legal rights or obligations of a party to a transaction
choice_b: Explain the general provisions of an approved form while completing it
choice_c: Deliver a completed approved form to a party
choice_d: Negotiate the business terms of a transaction
explanation: REEB 16.05 prohibits a licensee from giving advice or opinions about the legal rights or obligations of a party to a transaction -- effectively barring the unauthorized practice of law within an offer-to-purchase transaction.

question: REEB 16.05's prohibition on giving legal advice includes a narrow exception allowing a licensee to:
choice_a: Draft custom contract language for a party
choice_b: Give a general explanation of the provisions of an approved form when completing or delivering it
choice_c: Represent a party in a legal dispute over the contract
choice_d: Certify the legal sufficiency of a title
explanation: REEB 16.05 carves out one exception to its no-legal-advice rule: a licensee may give a general explanation of the provisions of an approved form while completing or delivering it.

question: Under REEB 16.05, may a licensee charge a separate fee just for completing an approved offer-to-purchase form?
choice_a: Yes, if disclosed to the client in advance
choice_b: Yes, but only for commercial transactions
choice_c: No, licensees may not charge a separate fee for completing an approved form
choice_d: Yes, but only with the Real Estate Examining Board's pre-approval
explanation: REEB 16.05 prohibits charging a separate fee solely for completing an approved form -- completing the form is considered part of the licensee's normal brokerage service.

question: When a firm reproduces a board-approved form for its own use, REEB 16.06 requires that the reproduction:
choice_a: May renumber lines for the firm's own formatting preference
choice_b: May omit any provisions the firm considers unnecessary
choice_c: May use a different font family without any restriction on size or margins
choice_d: Preserve identical line numbering and content as the board-approved original
explanation: REEB 16.06 requires a reproduced approved form to preserve identical line numbering and content as the original; only margin and font-size changes are permitted.

question: Under REEB 16.06, when reproducing an approved form, a firm:
choice_a: May not omit optional provisions or blank lines from the approved form
choice_b: May freely delete any optional clause it dislikes
choice_c: Must remove all blank lines to save paper
choice_d: May only reproduce half of the form's pages
explanation: REEB 16.06 prohibits omitting optional provisions or blank lines when a firm reproduces an approved form -- the reproduction must match the approved form's full content.

question: REEB 16.06 requires a firm that reproduces an approved form to include which of the following on the reproduction?
choice_a: The listing agent's personal cell phone number only
choice_b: The firm's name, address, and phone number
choice_c: The buyer's Social Security number
choice_d: A notarized signature block
explanation: REEB 16.06 requires the reproducing firm to identify itself on the reproduced form with its name, address, and phone number.

question: REEB 16.06 requires a reproduced approved form to retain:
choice_a: The signature of the Real Estate Examining Board's chairperson
choice_b: A blank space reserved for future board approval
choice_c: The board's approval statement and approval date
choice_d: A watermark unique to each individual licensee
explanation: REEB 16.06 requires that the board's approval statement and the approval date be retained on any reproduction of an approved form.

question: Under REEB 16.06, forms approved under REEB 16.03(1)(a)-(b), such as State Bar of Wisconsin deed and mortgage forms:
choice_a: May be modified freely by any attorney
choice_b: May be modified only with the client's written consent
choice_c: May be modified if the firm discloses the change to both parties
choice_d: May not be modified at all
explanation: REEB 16.06 singles out forms approved under REEB 16.03(1)(a)-(b) as forms that may not be modified at all, reflecting their especially standardized, legally reviewed content.

question: If a licensee needs to add a provision not found on an approved form, REEB 16.06 requires that the additional provision be:
choice_a: Placed on a separate addendum rather than altering the approved form itself
choice_b: Handwritten directly into the margin of the approved form
choice_c: Communicated to the other party orally instead of in writing
choice_d: Left out entirely, since no additions are ever permitted
explanation: REEB 16.06 requires additional provisions to be placed on an addendum rather than altering the approved form's own content or layout -- this is why WB-series offers use separate addenda for extra terms.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 706.02(1)(a), a valid conveyance -- including an accepted offer to purchase -- must:
choice_a: Be notarized by a licensed attorney
choice_b: Identify the parties to the transaction
choice_c: Include a legal opinion on marketable title
choice_d: Be recorded within 24 hours of signing
explanation: Wis. Stat. 706.02(1)(a) requires that a valid conveyance identify the parties -- one of the formal requisites that applies to an offer to purchase as a "contract to convey" real estate.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 706.02(1)(b), what must a valid offer to purchase identify?
choice_a: The buyer's lender
choice_b: The seller's attorney
choice_c: The land being conveyed
choice_d: The listing firm's commission rate
explanation: Wis. Stat. 706.02(1)(b) requires a valid conveyance to identify the land -- without an adequate legal description or identification of the property, the offer fails this formal requisite.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 706.02(1)(c), a valid offer to purchase must identify the interest conveyed and:
choice_a: The buyer's employer
choice_b: The seller's tax bracket
choice_c: The name of the title insurance company
choice_d: Any material term, condition, reservation, exception, or contingency affecting the interest
explanation: Wis. Stat. 706.02(1)(c) requires identification of the interest conveyed along with any material term, condition, reservation, exception, or contingency on which the interest arises, continues, or is extinguished, limited, or encumbered.

question: Because an offer to purchase is a "contract to convey" real estate, Wis. Stat. 706.02(1)(e) requires that it be signed by:
choice_a: All parties to the transaction -- both buyer and seller -- not just the grantor
choice_b: Only the seller, as the grantor of the property
choice_c: Only the buyer, as the party making the offer
choice_d: Only the listing agent, on behalf of both parties
explanation: While most conveyances need only the grantor's signature, Wis. Stat. 706.02(1)(e) requires that a lease or contract to convey -- which includes an accepted offer to purchase -- be signed by all parties, meaning both buyer and seller must sign for it to be enforceable.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 706.02(1)(f), if a conveyance alienates a married person's interest in a homestead, the conveyance generally requires:
choice_a: Court approval before either spouse signs
choice_b: The signature of each spouse, subject to limited statutory exceptions
choice_c: No spousal signature, only the titled owner's signature
choice_d: Approval from the Real Estate Examining Board
explanation: Wis. Stat. 706.02(1)(f) requires the signature of each spouse when a conveyance alienates any interest of a married person in a homestead, with narrow statutory exceptions such as certain mortgages and interspousal conveyances.

question: Wis. Stat. 706.02(1)(g) lists delivery as a formal requisite of a valid conveyance. What does this mean for an offer to purchase?
choice_a: The offer must be delivered by certified mail only
choice_b: Delivery is optional if both parties later ratify the agreement verbally
choice_c: The signed document generally must be delivered to be legally effective
choice_d: Delivery may occur only through a licensed attorney
explanation: Wis. Stat. 706.02(1)(g) requires delivery of a conveyance for it to be effective; a signed but undelivered offer or acceptance has not satisfied this formal requisite.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 706.02(2), how can an offer to purchase and its addenda or counter-offer together satisfy the writing requirements of ch. 706?
choice_a: They cannot; each separate document must independently satisfy every requirement on its own
choice_b: Only if a court later consolidates them into one document
choice_c: Only if all documents are signed on the exact same calendar day
choice_d: Through multiple writings that show mutual reference to one another or are physically annexed together
explanation: Wis. Stat. 706.02(2) allows the formal requisites of ch. 706 to be satisfied by several writings that show mutual reference to each other, or that are physically annexed together -- the legal basis for tying addenda and a counter-offer to the original offer to purchase.

question: If a buyer under an accepted Wisconsin offer to purchase (or a land contract) fails to record the document, what risk does Wis. Stat. 706.08(1)(a) create?
choice_a: A later good-faith purchaser for value who records first can take priority over the buyer's unrecorded interest
choice_b: The offer becomes void immediately upon acceptance
choice_c: The seller automatically forfeits the earnest money
choice_d: The buyer loses the right to sue the seller for breach of contract
explanation: Wis. Stat. 706.08(1)(a) makes an unrecorded conveyance void as against a subsequent good-faith purchaser for value who records first -- giving a buyer a legal-effect reason to record an accepted offer or land contract even though recording is not itself required to form the contract.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 788.015, parties to a Wisconsin real estate transaction may:
choice_a: Never agree to arbitrate a dispute arising from the transaction
choice_b: Agree in writing to arbitrate disputes arising from the real estate transaction
choice_c: Arbitrate a dispute only if the Real Estate Examining Board orders it
choice_d: Arbitrate only commission disputes, never disputes between buyer and seller
explanation: Wis. Stat. 788.015 authorizes parties to a real estate transaction to agree in writing to arbitrate disputes arising from that transaction -- part of the contracts curriculum underlying offer-to-purchase practice.
